title: Capacitors, Magnetic Fields and Induction
seo_title: Year 13 A Level Physics: Capacitors and Magnetic Fields Worksheets
standard_code: A level Physics: Fields and their consequences
standard_text: Capacitance, energy stored by a capacitor, charging and discharging through a resistor and the time constant; magnetic flux density, force on a current-carrying wire and on a moving charge, electromagnetic induction and transformers.
meta_desc: Free Year 13 A level physics worksheets on capacitors and magnetic fields: Q = CV, energy stored, the time constant RC, F = BIL, F = BQv, flux linkage, Faraday's law and transformers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Q = CV; E = ½CV²; τ = RC.
key_sub: ε = NΔΦ/Δt; F = BIL; F = BQv.
body_html:
How to think about it

A capacitor stores charge Q = CV and energy ½QV = ½CV². Discharging through a resistor, Q = Q₀e−t/RC; the time constant RC is the time to fall to 37%.

In a magnetic field a wire feels F = BIL and a moving charge F = BQv. A changing flux linkage induces an e.m.f.: ε = NΔΦ/Δt. For an ideal transformer Vs/Vp = Ns/Np.

Example

470 μF charged to 12 V. Energy?

½ × 470 × 10−6 × 12²

Answer: 0.0338 J

Example

100-turn coil, Φ falls by 0.002 Wb in 0.05 s. e.m.f.?

100 × 0.002 ÷ 0.05

Answer: 4.0 V

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to change μF into F.
  • Using E = CV² without the half.
  • Missing the number of turns N.

faq.q: What is the time constant of a capacitor circuit?
faq.a: RC: the time for the charge (or current or p.d.) to fall to 1/e, about 37%, of its starting value.
The induced e.m.f. equals the rate of change of flux linkage: ε = NΔΦ/Δt.
